title: tRPC WebSocket transport is exempt from the dashboard-key check, so a bare session cookie drives the entire admin API (host root)
summary: `isAuthed` skips the CSRF/replay `verifyCsrf` check whenever the request arrived over the WebSocket transport, and the tRPC v11 WS handler serves `query` and `mutation` — not just subscriptions — so possession of the session cookie alone is sufficient to call every protected procedure.

title: A corrupt/truncated TLS cert or key puts the core into a permanent boot crash-loop that neither Update nor Repair fixes
summary: ensureCert() only tests file EXISTENCE and loadCert() only reads bytes, so a present-but-invalid cert/key reaches `Fastify({https})`, which throws synchronously OUTSIDE the try/catch that was meant to fall back to plain HTTP — main() rejects, process.exit(1), and `restart: unless-stopped` loops forever.

title: Install-time compose gate compares un-normalized host paths — `//run:/hostrun` mounts the Docker socket with zero warnings
summary: `checkHostPath` string-matches a raw bind source against SENSITIVE_ROOTS without canonicalizing it, so a duplicated leading slash (`//run`) or a `/./` segment (`/./root`) defeats every sensitive-path check while Linux still resolves the mount to the real directory.

title: A leading `~` in a bind source is never expanded, so `~/.ssh:/x` mounts the host root account's home past the `/root` check
summary: `checkHostPath` early-returns on any source that does not start with `/`, treating `~/.ssh` as a harmless in-app-folder relative path — but `docker compose` expands `~` to $HOME before handing the path to the daemon, so the mount lands on the host's `/root`.

title: Five third-party GitHub Actions pinned to mutable major tags in the job that publishes the root-privileged core image
summary: The `build` job holds `packages: write`, logs into ghcr.io and publishes `:latest`, yet every docker/* action it runs is referenced by a mutable major tag rather than a commit SHA — unlike cla.yml, which the project does pin.

title: Runtime base image is Node 20, which is past end-of-life, and is pinned by mutable tag with no digest
summary: Both build and runtime stages use `FROM node:20-alpine`. Node.js 20 ('Iron') reached end-of-life on 2026-04-30; today is 2026-07-30, so the image line that runs the root + docker.sock daemon no longer receives Node, V8, OpenSSL or Alpine-userland security rebuilds.

title: Session cookie is transmitted in cleartext to the plain-HTTP front door on every visit to the http:// URL the installer advertises; no HSTS anywhere
summary: The session cookie is not `Secure` by default, so the browser attaches it to plain-HTTP requests to port 80 — which is exactly the URL the installer tells the admin to open — and no `Strict-Transport-Security` header exists to stop that first cleartext hop.

title: Backup restore is fully unauthenticated whenever no admin exists, so an unclaimed (or de-claimed) box can be provisioned by any LAN visitor
summary: Both the restore upload and the restore-run WebSocket skip auth and CSRF entirely when `isConfigured()` is false, letting an unauthenticated LAN client replace the whole `config/` tree (admin credential, terminal toggles, Cloudflare tunnel token) on a box that has no admin yet.

title: First-run admin creation (auth.setup) is a public procedure — an unclaimed box belongs to the first LAN visitor (confirmed)
summary: `auth.setup` is a `publicProcedure` guarded only by `isConfigured()`, so from the moment install.sh finishes until a human opens the dashboard, any device on the LAN can create the admin account.

title: system.addSshKey turns any dashboard session into permanent host root — no Advanced toggle, no key list, no revocation, survives password reset and uninstall
summary: `system.addSshKey` appends an attacker-supplied public key to the HOST's `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` via a helper container that bind-mounts `/root`, and unlike the root terminal and app shells it is behind no Advanced setting and has no way to see or remove what was added.

title: The file explorer's sandbox root is the data dir, so the core's own docker-compose.yml is admin-writable and the updater then executes it — bypassing the compose consent gate
summary: `ROOT = path.resolve(DATA_DIR)` puts `/data/docker-compose.yml` — the descriptor the update helper runs with `docker compose up -d --force-recreate` — inside the file explorer's writable sandbox, and that file is never risk-checked by `compose-validate.ts`.

title: The update has no rollback and retains no known-good image; a bad :latest bricks the dashboard, and "Free up space" deletes the only local rollback candidate
summary: `runUpdate` pulls `:latest` and force-recreates the core with no health gate, no previous-version pin and no rollback path; if the new image fails to boot, `restart: unless-stopped` crash-loops it and the dashboard is gone until a human with a keyboard arrives.

title: The OTA update payload is neither signed at publish nor verified at pull — TLS to GHCR is the only integrity control
summary: The one-click self-update pulls a mutable tag and runs it as root with the Docker socket, with no signature, attestation, or digest check anywhere in the publish or install path.

title: Restore has no busy guard and replaces config/ and apps/ non-atomically, so a concurrent run or a power cut mid-restore deletes the admin credential and every platform secret
summary: runRestore does `fs.rmSync(dest, {recursive:true, force:true})` then `fs.renameSync(src, dest)` for config/ and apps/ with nothing serialising concurrent restores — unlike backup, which has an explicit `running` flag and BackupBusyError.

title: Every third-party action in the image-publishing job is pinned to a mutable tag, including the one handed the registry token
summary: The job that builds and pushes the OTA image references five docker/* actions and two actions/* actions by floating major tag, so an upstream tag move executes attacker code inside the job holding `packages: write`.

title: Every platform secret rides inside the backup tarball unencrypted — including the credential for the backup destination itself, contradicting a documented guarantee in docs/SECURITY.md
summary: backupStream() tars config/ wholesale, so the Stripe live keys, SMTP password/Resend key, Cloudflare tunnel token, dashboard TLS private key, admin password hash, every app's Fabric secret, and rclone.conf itself are written into an unencrypted archive that is then uploaded off-site on a schedule.

title: /api/fabric/stripe?account= lets any stripe-capable app read EVERY configured Stripe account's live keys
summary: The Fabric Stripe endpoint authorizes only on the boolean `app.stripe` capability and then returns whichever account the caller names in the query string, with no binding between an app and the account(s) it was installed for.

title: readJson fails open on ANY read error, so an unreadable auth.json silently reverts an established install to an unclaimed first-run box — and the claim then destroys the real credential
summary: readJson's bare `catch { return fallback; }` cannot distinguish "file absent" from "file corrupt / EIO / EACCES", so a single failed read of auth.json at module load leaves `username: null, passwordHash: null`, making `isConfigured()` false — which re-opens the entire first-run trust window on a long-configured masjid, including the unauthenticated restore endpoints.

title: The only two internet-reachable routes are unauthenticated, unrate-limited, and do a synchronous multi-hundred-KB disk read per request
summary: `/api/public/appearance` and `/api/public/logo` are deliberately exempt from the tunnel guard and are the only routes served publicly, yet they are the only Fabric handlers that never call `fabricRateOk`, and each request performs blocking `fs.readFileSync` calls (branding.json plus the up-to-1 MB logo) on the single event loop.

title: auth.login has no arrival cap and a FIFO verify mutex, so an unauthenticated LAN flood locks the real admin out of their own dashboard
summary: Login serialises every argon2 verify through a promise chain but never limits how many requests may enter that chain (the hard lockout is off by default), so an attacker can queue an unbounded backlog of verifies that the admin's own correct attempt must wait behind.

title: An unclaimed or auth-reset box lets any LAN visitor claim the admin account and also upload+run a backup restore unauthenticated (previously accepted — independently confirmed, with the restore path as an addition)
summary: While no admin exists, auth.setup is open (known TOFU window) and so are /api/restore/upload and /api/restore/run — so an unauthenticated LAN party can either take ownership of the box or replace config/, apps/ and every app volume with an archive of their choosing.

title: The compose risk gate's own "DO NOT REGRESS" checks have zero test coverage
summary: compose-guard.test.ts tests only the v0.45.0 external-volume/external-network refusals; none of the §15 checks that actually stop an app from escaping its container are exercised by any test.

title: Any stripe-capable app can read every Stripe account's secret keys via /api/fabric/stripe?account=
summary: The endpoint authorises on "does this app hold the `stripe` capability", then resolves whatever account name the request asks for, with no per-app scoping of which account it may read.

title: Abandoned WebSocket upgrades on the HTTP front door leak sockets forever — unauthenticated remote resource exhaustion
summary: The ingress `upgrade` listener returns without destroying the socket when the request path is not a routed app, so every such upgrade request permanently pins a file descriptor and socket in the core container.

title: SENSITIVE_ROOTS matches descendants only, so mounting `/opt` — the parent of the platform's own data dir — is unflagged
summary: The list entry `/opt/openmasjid` is compared with an equals-or-descendant test, so a bind mount of the strict ancestor `/opt` grants the whole platform data directory it was added to protect, with no warning.

title: An unpinned Docker Hub `alpine` image is executed --privileged --pid=host and chrooted into the host root filesystem
summary: The host-reboot helper runs `docker run --rm --privileged --pid=host alpine chroot /proc/1/root /bin/sh -c ...`. The image reference is the bare string `alpine`, which resolves to the mutable `docker.io/library/alpine:latest` — no tag, no digest, no content-trust verification — for the single highest-privilege operation in the product.

title: Community app-store archives are fetched over plain HTTP with no integrity check, and the retrieved compose becomes a running container
summary: `community.addRepo` accepts any `z.string().url()`, including `http://`, and the archive fetcher explicitly permits the `http:` scheme and switches to the plain-HTTP module — so app definitions that become containers on the masjid's host arrive over an unauthenticated, unverified channel.

title: Online admin-password guessing is capped only by serialized argon2 (~10-20 attempts/sec), with no lockout by default and no failed-login alert
summary: The growing failure delay is awaited after the verify mutex has been released, so concurrent attempts' delays overlap and impose no throughput limit; the only real cap is one argon2id verify at a time, and the hard cooldown is off by default.

title: Per-app .env — which carries OPENMASJID_APP_SECRET — is written world-readable, while its twin meta.json holding the same secret is written 0600
summary: writeEnvFile uses a bare fs.writeFileSync (mode 0666 & ~umask → 0644) for apps/<id>/.env, whereas saveMeta routes apps/<id>/meta.json through writeJson, which deliberately forces 0600 for exactly this class of secret.

title: recreateCore reports success from `docker run -d`'s exit code, so a failed update or restore tells the admin "restarting now" and destroys its own logs
summary: `recreateCore` returns `code === 0` from a detached `docker run -d`, which only reports that the helper *launched*; whether the inner `docker compose up -d --force-recreate` succeeded is never observed, and `--rm` deletes the helper so its output is unrecoverable.

title: Every platform secret is plaintext on an unencrypted filesystem, with no documented physical-trust assumption for a wall-mounted box
summary: `config/` holds the Stripe secret keys, the Cloudflare tunnel token, SMTP/Resend credentials, the rclone backup credentials, the TLS private key and the admin argon2 hash as plaintext files whose only protection is POSIX mode — which is worth nothing to someone who removes the SD card or boots a USB.

title: The file explorer returns every platform secret to the browser, contradicting the "never returned to the UI" invariant the credential stores are built around
summary: `files.read` and `/api/files/download` are rooted at DATA_DIR with no deny-list, so `config/stripe.json`, `config/email.json`, `config/cloudflare/.env`, `config/rclone.conf`, `config/tls/key.pem` and `config/auth.json` are all readable verbatim through the dashboard.

title: Restore extracts with --no-same-permissions and then moves the tree into place, so config/ and apps/ come back with umask modes and APPS_DIR permanently loses its 0750
summary: The restore tar drops the archived file modes in favour of the process umask, and the staged directories are renamed over /data/config and /data/apps — so secret files land 0644 and apps/ becomes 0755 with nothing in the core ever re-tightening it.

title: The one-click update can silently downgrade, and a bad release has no rollback or in-product recovery
summary: runUpdate pulls `:latest` and force-recreates the core without comparing versions before or after, records no previous image or digest, and the documented fallback (re-run the installer) re-pulls the same tag.

title: install.sh silently grants the invoking user permanent host-root-equivalent via the docker group, and uninstall never revokes it
summary: When run via sudo, the installer adds SUDO_USER to the docker group without asking; docker group membership is equivalent to root, and do_uninstall does not remove it.

title: The dev-mode data directory `.data/` is excluded by neither .gitignore nor .dockerignore
summary: config.ts falls back to a `.data` directory under the process cwd for local dev, and that path is in no ignore file — so a maintainer's admin hash, payment keys, tunnel token and TLS key are one `git add -A` from a public repo, and one local `npm run image` from a published layer.

title: App-raised Fabric alerts are billed to the platform's own email budget, so one chatty app both spams the admin and silences the OS's real alerts
summary: deliverAlert always passes the literal `'os'` as the rate-limit key to sendBrandedEmail, even when `input.source` is an installed app id, so an app's alert emails consume the platform's 30/min bucket instead of its own.

title: Every config cache fails open to defaults on a corrupt read, and the next write persists those defaults — permanently losing Stripe keys, SMTP credentials, the tunnel domain and the backup destination
summary: settings.json, stripe.json and email.json are each read once at module load through readJson's swallow-everything catch into a module-level `cache`; a failed read silently yields defaults, and the first subsequent write flushes those defaults over the real file.

title: When the backend is unreachable the dashboard shows the first-run "create your admin account" screen, complete with an unauthenticated restore-from-backup control
summary: Root treats a FAILED `auth.me` query identically to a successful "setup required" response — `!data` falls into the same branch and `setupRequired` defaults to true — and `retry: false` means a single network blip is enough.

title: No response-size cap on any outbound fetch: a spoofed or compromised catalog can OOM the core on a Raspberry Pi
summary: The catalog, changelog and version fetches all buffer the entire response body before any limit is applied — `res.json()` with no cap, and `(await res.text()).slice(0, MAX_BYTES)` where the slice happens after the whole body is already in memory.

title: The file explorer is entirely synchronous with no pagination, so one large folder blocks the event loop that also serves the public app ingress
summary: listDir does a blocking readdirSync followed by one blocking lstatSync per entry with no cap or paging, and removeEntry does a blocking recursive rmSync — all on the daemon's single main thread.

title: The /trpc origin guard compares the raw URL with startsWith, and the router accepts a percent-encoded spelling that walks past it
summary: `req.url.startsWith('/trpc')` is exactly the raw-string URL comparison CLAUDE.md §15 forbids after v0.46.0; Fastify dispatches `/%74rpc/auth.login` to the tRPC route while the hook's check returns false.

title: Backup stages a full copy of every app volume onto the same disk with no free-space precheck, unlike restore
summary: stageVolumes tars each app volume into DATA_DIR/.backup-staging before streaming the archive, with no check that the copies will fit — while system/restore.ts does exactly that check with statfsSync before extracting.

title: Outbound SMTP never requires TLS, so a STARTTLS-stripping peer or MITM gets the masjid's mail credential and every outbound message body
summary: Both the SMTP sender and the verify path build a nodemailer transport with secure:false (the default, port 587) and never set requireTLS, so if the server does not advertise STARTTLS the connection — including AUTH — proceeds in plaintext.

title: Verify-before-save exfiltrates the stored SMTP password to any host the caller names, defeating the write-only secret
summary: email.save merges the retained SMTP password into the previewed config and then authenticates against the newly-supplied host before persisting, so submitting a new host with a blank password makes the platform log in to an attacker-chosen server with the masjid's stored credential.

title: startApp runs `docker compose up` on the on-disk compose with no risk gate, so a writable compose is host root
summary: Every other path that starts a stack re-runs checkCompose (install, updateCatalogApp, reupAllApps), but startApp composes up whatever is on disk unchecked — and the compose file is writable through the File Explorer.

title: prefers-reduced-motion is not honoured for any JS-driven animation — Motion defaults to "never"
summary: No <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"> is rendered anywhere, and Motion's context default is reducedMotion: "never", so every spring/transform animation runs at full amplitude for a user who has asked for reduced motion.

title: RTL and translation are unreachable at runtime: there is no language selector, and the strings for one are orphaned
summary: prefs.language is initialised to 'en' and nothing in the UI ever changes it, so applyLanguage()'s dir=rtl branch can never fire; the en.json keys for the missing picker (including native Arabic and Urdu labels) are dead.

title: No Arabic/Naskh font is bundled and the font stack has no Arabic fallback
summary: Only Inter and Space Grotesk are self-hosted, with latin/latin-ext/cyrillic/greek/vietnamese subsets — no Arabic coverage — and --font-sans falls back only to generic system faces.

title: Every stats subscriber runs its own 2-second collector, and each tick spawns processes including a blocking execSync
summary: stats.stream is a per-subscription async generator with no shared snapshot, and collectStats() calls si.fsSize(), which on Linux runs execSync('cat /proc/mounts') plus exec('df …') — so N open dashboards multiply subprocess spawns and Docker API calls linearly, forever.

title: A failed scheduled backup resets the schedule clock, so there is no retry until the next full interval
summary: record() writes lastRunAt on failure as well as success, and tick() gates the next run on lastRunAt, so one transient failure defers the next attempt by a whole day (or week).

title: Authentication and session handling have no tests at all
summary: None of the 12 enumerated test files touches auth/passwords.ts, auth/sessions.ts, auth/store.ts or trpc/routers/auth.ts, so no test pins argon2id, session expiry, the CSRF dashboard-key comparison, or the first-run compare-and-set.

title: The file-explorer path sandbox — a documented security guarantee — has no tests
summary: files/manager.ts (243 lines) implements traversal and symlink-escape containment with a subtle parent-resolve argument, and no test exercises any of it.

title: The backup/restore invariants that §15 documents at length have no tests
summary: backup.ts (261 lines), backup-upload.ts (284) and restore.ts (264) are untested, including the ok-accounting rules and the writeFailed-vs-exit-code distinction that §15 calls out by name.

title: Off-site and manual backups archive every platform secret and app volume with no encryption at rest or in transit
summary: backupStream() produces a plain gzipped tar (no encryption) that bundles config/ (auth.json argon2 hash, stripe.json secret+webhook keys, email.json SMTP/Resend secret, cloudflare/.env tunnel token, tls/key.pem private key, settings.json webhook URL) and every app data volume (donations records, the Students app's minors' PII), and runBackup streams it verbatim to a third-party remote (Google Drive / NAS / SFTP / SMB / WebDAV) via `rclone rcat`.

title: Ingress WebSocket upgrade tunnels the raw socket unconditionally, so a pipelined second request bypasses both the LAN-only /fabric refusal and the X-Forwarded-* sanitisation
summary: The front door's `upgrade` handler connects to the app port, writes the request, and pipes both directions without ever requiring a 101 response, so the connection becomes a raw TCP tunnel to the app even when the app answered with an ordinary keep-alive HTTP response.

title: Per-app HTTPS port allocation ignores ports already published on the host, so another app can occupy the port the dashboard's "Open" link for a payment app points at
summary: `pickHttpsPort()` avoids only other apps' recorded `httpsPort` and live proxy ports — never the host's actually-listening/published ports — and `ensureProxy` records the proxy in its map synchronously even when `server.listen` fails with EADDRINUSE, so a Stripe app can be assigned a port that belongs to a different container.

title: startApp() runs docker compose up on an on-disk compose file without re-running the install-time risk gate
summary: Install, update and post-restore reup all call `checkCompose` first; `startApp` does not, so any path that starts an existing app trusts whatever `apps/<id>/compose.yml` currently says.

title: App containers get no least-privilege hardening from the platform
summary: The platform writes the app's compose verbatim and runs `docker compose up`; it never injects `user:`, `cap_drop`, `security_opt: no-new-privileges`, `read_only`, or a pids/memory limit, so every app runs as root inside its container with Docker's full default capability set.

title: Backups are unencrypted and a torn live SQLite capture still exits tar 0
summary: The archive that carries every platform secret and all app data is a plain gzipped tar with no encryption, and app volumes are tarred while their containers run, so `ok: true` is not evidence the databases inside will open.

title: Forged client IP: `cf-connecting-ip` is trusted unconditionally, so any LAN client can dictate the `X-Forwarded-For` the platform presents to every app
summary: Both reverse proxies derive the "trusted" client IP from the client-supplied `cf-connecting-ip` header without checking whether the request actually arrived over the Cloudflare tunnel, and never strip that header, so a direct caller on the LAN chooses the IP every app sees.

title: An app's LAN-only `/fabric/*` is reachable over the public Cloudflare tunnel by changing the case of one letter
summary: `isFabricSubpath` compares the path segment to the literal lowercase `'fabric'` and does not normalise dot segments, so `/donate/FABRIC/...` and `/donate/./fabric/...` are proxied to the app instead of being refused, defeating the documented "an app's /fabric/* is never reachable over the tunnel" wall.

title: startApp() runs `docker compose up` on the on-disk compose file without re-running the risk gate
summary: Every other path that starts a compose project re-vets the file (install, update, post-restore reup), but startApp reads whatever is on disk and brings it up unchecked.

title: Unbounded serialized argon2 queue lets an unauthenticated login flood block the admin out of the dashboard
summary: Every credential check is forced through one global promise-chain mutex with no cap on how many attempts may be queued, so an unauthenticated flood of wrong-password attempts puts the admin's own login at the back of an arbitrarily long queue.

title: email.save re-uses the stored SMTP password against an attacker-chosen host, turning a write-only secret into a readable one
summary: A blank `smtp.pass` means "keep the stored password", but `smtp.host`/`port`/`user` can be changed in the same call, and the router then connects and authenticates to the new host with the retained password — so the secret is exfiltrated to whatever mail server the caller names.

title: Unrotated container logs plus a 1:1 unauthenticated log amplifier can fill the host disk
summary: The core service the installer generates configures no logging driver limits, so Docker's default json-file log grows without bound — and any unauthenticated LAN client can drive exactly one log line per HTTP request.

title: cloudflared runs from the mutable `:latest` tag while the adjacent comment claims the image is pinned
summary: The generated tunnel compose uses `image: cloudflare/cloudflared:latest` under a comment asserting that `--no-autoupdate` 'keeps the pinned image' — but `--no-autoupdate` only stops cloudflared replacing its own binary; the image reference itself is the most mutable form possible.

title: Two of the five open moderate advisories have no fix inside the declared semver ranges, and the CI audit gate is set to a level that can never fail on them
summary: The CI supply-chain gate runs `npm audit --audit-level=high`, so no moderate advisory in a runtime dependency can ever turn the build red — and for `uuid`/`dockerode` and `react-router-dom` the installed versions are already the newest their declared caret ranges permit, so npm's 'fix available via npm audit fix' is not achievable without a major bump.

title: The image build runs install scripts for three native/gRPC packages that exist only for dockerode features this codebase never uses
summary: `npm ci` in the build stage executes install scripts without `--ignore-scripts`; four packages in the tree declare them, and `protobufjs`, `ssh2` and the optional native `cpu-features` are present solely for dockerode transports (SSH, BuildKit gRPC, image builds) that the core never touches.

title: Off-site backup destination password is passed to rclone as a command-line argument, exposing it in the host process table
summary: `obscure()` spawns `rclone obscure <plaintext password>`, so the NAS/SFTP/Drive credential appears verbatim in the process argv for the lifetime of that spawn.

title: /api/health and /api/ready are registered on the tunnel-facing front door without the tunnel guard, publishing the exact core version to the internet
summary: Registered routes skip the front door's `notFoundHandler`, and `matchesSecretRoute` only covers `/api/auth/session` and `/api/fabric*`, so `/api/health` (which returns the version) and `/api/ready` are served unauthenticated to anyone who reaches the Cloudflare tunnel.

title: Privileged and host-mounting helper containers run unpinned public images pulled at the moment of use
summary: The reboot helper runs `--privileged --pid=host` and chroots into the host root from the floating tag `alpine`; the SSH-key helper mounts host `/root` from `alpine:3.20`; the tunnel runs `cloudflare/cloudflared:latest` — none pinned by digest, all pulled from Docker Hub on first use.

title: The installer implements none of its documented network provisioning and touches no firewall, while the docs and the TLS certificate advertise an address that will not resolve
summary: install.sh does no static-IP configuration, sets no hostname, installs no avahi/mDNS and configures no firewall — `grep -niE "avahi|hostnamectl|netplan|nmcli|dhcpcd|systemd-networkd|ufw|firewall|iptables|mdns" install.sh` returns zero hits — yet docs/NETWORKING.md tells the volunteer the installer offers all of it and the self-signed certificate is issued for `openmasjidos.local`.

title: index.ts re-implements the tunnel check inline, dropping the v0.46.0 header normalization, and 308-redirects to a client-controlled Host
summary: The front-door notFoundHandler compares x-forwarded-proto with a raw `=== 'https'` instead of calling the shared isViaTunnel helper, and then builds a redirect target straight from the request's Host header.

title: The Content-Security-Policy is frame-ancestors only — no default-src or script-src on the dashboard
summary: The onSend hook sets a CSP consisting solely of `frame-ancestors 'self'`, so the dashboard has no script-source, connect, or object restriction to contain an injection.

title: The Cloudflare tunnel token is interpolated into the container's command line instead of passed as an environment variable
summary: The generated compose uses `command: tunnel --no-autoupdate run --token ${CF_TUNNEL_TOKEN}`, so docker compose interpolates the secret from the env file into Config.Cmd, making it visible in `docker inspect` and in the host's process table.

title: The app-offline alert has no cooldown or dedupe, so a flapping app emails the admin every minute indefinitely
summary: The monitor fires on every running→stopped transition it observes on its 60 s poll with no per-app cooldown, unlike the update monitor which tracks what it has already alerted about.

title: startApp failures are swallowed when toggling an app's internet exposure, so the admin sees success while the app is down or still advertising a stale public URL
summary: Both exposure-related reup paths use `startApp(id).catch(() => {})` and then return a success payload, so a failed compose up is invisible to the admin.

title: Every OS alert email carries the masjid's private LAN address and exact platform version through a third-party mail path
summary: brandedEmail builds its action link from desiredBaseUrl(), which is an RFC1918 http:// URL, and the OS alert copy puts the running and available version numbers in the body — all of which transits Resend or the masjid's SMTP provider in plaintext.

title: The Fabric per-IP rate limiter collapses to a single shared bucket because every app container appears as the docker bridge gateway (previously accepted — independently confirmed)
summary: The limiter on the secret-gated Fabric routes keys on req.ip, but app containers reach the platform through Docker's bridge gateway, so all of them share one 120-requests-per-minute bucket.

title: The learned platform address trusts a request's Host header, and the comment's safety argument is incorrect
summary: observeDashboardHost() persists any IPv4-literal Host header from a session-authenticated request as the address handed to every installed app, on the stated grounds that an attacker cannot make it point elsewhere — but the Host header is arbitrary and independent of where the request was actually delivered.

title: Literal control bytes in notify/alerts.ts make grep, ripgrep and git grep skip the whole file
summary: A regex character class was saved with raw 0x00, 0x1F and 0x7F bytes instead of \u escapes, so every grep-family tool classifies the file as binary and reports "Binary file … matches" with no lines.

title: shadcn/ui and Radix are documented as the component layer but are absent; the hand-rolled Modal has no focus management
summary: No Radix or shadcn code is in the repo, and the replacement Modal declares aria-modal="true" without a focus trap, initial focus, focus restore, or aria-labelledby.

title: Four copies of the same rate limiter and two copies of the security-invariant header drop-set
summary: The forwarding-header strip list that §15 calls a hostile-boundary invariant is duplicated verbatim in two proxies, and the fixed-window rate limiter is reimplemented four times with inconsistent eviction.

title: The timezone and 12/24-hour display preferences are only applied to the clock widget
summary: CLAUDE.md §13.1 says these preferences govern the timestamps and log times shown in the dashboard, but every other timestamp uses bare toLocaleString()/toLocaleDateString(), ignoring both.

title: Hardcoded English aria-labels bypass i18next
summary: Five accessible names are English string literals rather than t() calls, in violation of §15's "no hardcoded English in components".

title: isNewerVersion misreads semver prereleases, so a prerelease is offered as a stable update
summary: Both copies of the comparator parseInt each dotted segment, so "1.0.1-alpha" parses as 1.0.1 and compares as a newer release than 1.0.0.

title: The published Docker image ships AGPL-licensed code with no copy of the AGPL-3.0 text
summary: The runtime stage copies package.json, VERSION, the two dist trees and node_modules, but never the repo-root LICENSE, so the image conveyed to ghcr.io contains no license text for the project's own code.

title: isFabricSubpath normalises percent-escapes but not dot segments, so /donate/./fabric/... is not refused over the tunnel
summary: The predicate splits on `/` and compares segments, but `.` and `..` are ordinary segments to it, so a dot-segment spelling of an app's LAN-only /fabric path is classified as an ordinary app path and proxied verbatim.

title: Backup destination fields are written into rclone.conf without a newline check, allowing arbitrary rclone config injection
summary: `setDestination` builds rclone.conf by string-concatenating admin-supplied `host`, `user`, `url`, `vendor` and `share` values into `key = value` lines; none is checked for `\n`, so a value can append additional config keys or whole `[section]` blocks.

title: CasaOS repo SSRF allowlist misses non-canonical IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals and several reserved ranges
summary: `ipIsPrivate` recognises only the `::ffff:d.d.d.d` spelling of a mapped address, so `[::ffff:7f00:1]` and `[0:0:0:0:0:ffff:127.0.0.1]` are classified as public and pinned straight into the socket; 100.64.0.0/10 and other reserved ranges are absent too.

title: install.sh implements none of the documented network setup, and README advertises a "Reconfigure network" menu entry that does not exist
summary: CLAUDE.md §8.2 steps 4-5 require the installer to offer a static IP and to set the hostname plus avahi so the dashboard answers at `openmasjidos.local`; install.sh does neither, and its management menu offers "Reset sign-in" where the README documents "Reconfigure network".

title: The ingress reverse proxy never tears down the upstream connection when the client goes away
summary: `proxyHttp` sets no timeout on the upstream request and installs no close handler, so when a client disconnects mid-response the upstream socket to the app container is unpiped but never destroyed.

title: Orphan recovery derives an app's "catalog" kind — and therefore its default internet exposure — from an app-controlled Docker label
summary: `listInstalled` recovers a metadata-less omos-* project using the `com.openmasjid.kind` container label, which the platform never sets and only ever reads, so the label is entirely app-supplied — yet it decides both the "Official" badge and, via isExposedMeta's catalog grandfather, whether the app is routed publicly over the tunnel.

title: Mounting the host /proc as ":ro" gives read-write access to the host root filesystem via /host/proc/1/root
summary: The `:ro` flag applies to the procfs mount, not to the magic /proc/<pid>/root symlinks it contains, so the comment's claim of read-only host visibility overstates the containment.

title: The installer pipes two remote scripts into a root shell with no checksum or signature
summary: Docker is installed by curl-ing get.docker.com straight into sh as root, and the installer itself is delivered the same way — HTTPS is the only integrity control on either.

title: eslint does not exist in this repo, so the documented definition of done is unachievable
summary: CLAUDE.md §16 documents `npm run lint` as "eslint + tsc --noEmit" and §17 requires eslint to be clean, but there is no eslint config, no eslint dependency, and both workspace lint scripts are tsc-only.

title: Version drift: CLAUDE.md §18 says 0.1.0, VERSION says 0.47.1, and three package.json files hardcode 0.2.0
summary: The document that declares VERSION the single source of truth states a current version 46 minors stale, and the three workspace manifests carry their own hardcoded version strings that §18 forbids.

title: The design system's masjid identity (emerald/gold) documented in §14 has been replaced by generic cyan/navy
summary: CLAUDE.md specifies a charcoal-green base with an emerald primary and a #D4AF37 gold accent; the shipped tokens are deep navy, cyan, and amber, and the accent palette has no emerald option at all.

title: §7's repository map no longer matches the tree, and the markdown files lack the SPDX header §19 mandates
summary: The documented directory layout is several refactors out of date — six core directories are undocumented and the tRPC routers moved — and six markdown files are missing the SPDX header the same document requires of every file.

title: God files: two source files over 1000 lines and three more over 400
summary: Settings.tsx is 1927 lines and apps/manager.ts is 1069; install.sh is 915 and app.css is 988.

title: Platform email copy is hardcoded English with no i18n in packages/core
summary: Alert emails, the test email, and every restore/update progress line are built from English string literals in the core, which has no i18next integration at all.

title: Stripe account removal fires on one click; the secret key is unrecoverable
summary: Remove button had no confirmation and identical styling to Edit 8px away.

title: The "also delete this app's data" checkbox stays ticked after Cancel
summary: Neither Cancel nor onClose reset deleteData, so reopening the dialog had permanent volume destruction pre-armed.

title: image-size JPEG marker walk does not stop at SOS
summary: On a malformed JPEG the walk enters entropy-coded data and can read a bit pattern as a frame header, returning wrong dimensions instead of null.
